patterns: what is a list in python

nums.append(4) adds an item
nums[0] gets the first item
Useful methods: append, remove, pop, sort, reverse, len().

patterns: what is a tuple in python
responses: A tuple is like a list but immutable (cannot be changed after creation): t = (1, 2, 3). Use tuples for fixed data; they are slightly faster and can be dictionary keys.

patterns: what is a dictionary in python
how to use dict in python

patterns: what is a set in python
responses: A set is an unordered collection of unique items: s = set([1, 2, 2, 3]) becomes 1, 2, 3. It supports union, intersection and difference. Quick trick to remove duplicates: list(set(my_list)).

patterns: difference between for and while loop

while x < 10: x += 1 runs while the condition is true.
break stops a loop, continue skips to the next round.

Call it with add(2, 3). Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values you pass.
A lambda is a small one-line anonymous function: square = lambda x: x * x. It is often used with map(), filter() and sorted(key=...).

patterns: what is a class in python

patterns: which programming language should i learn first
responses: Programming is writing instructions a computer can follow. To start: pick one language (Python is great for beginners), learn basics (variables, loops, functions), then build small projects every week.
An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure to solve a problem. Pseudocode describes it in plain language, and a flowchart shows it with diagrams.

A data structure is a way of organising data for efficient use. Common ones: array, linked list, stack, queue, hash table, tree, graph, heap. DSA = Data Structures and Algorithms, the base of coding interviews.
An array stores items in contiguous memory with fast index access O(1) but slow insertion. A linked list stores nodes connected by pointers, with fast insertion but slow search O(n).
Stack = LIFO (last in, first out), with push and pop; used in undo and recursion. Queue = FIFO (first in, first out), with enqueue and dequeue; used in scheduling and BFS.

patterns: what is a tree in data structure
what is a graph in data structure
responses: A tree is a hierarchy of nodes; a binary tree has at most 2 children per node and a BST keeps left < root < right. A graph is nodes plus edges. BFS explores level by level (queue); DFS goes deep first (stack or recursion).

A hash table maps keys to values using a hash function, giving average O(1) lookup. When two keys land in the same slot it is a collision, handled by chaining or open addressing. Python dict is a hash table.
Sorting arranges data in order. Simple: bubble, selection, insertion (O(n^2)). Efficient: merge sort and quick sort (O(n log n)). In Python just use sorted() or list.sort().
Linear search checks items one by one: O(n). Binary search halves a sorted list each step: O(log n). It needs sorted data.
Big O describes how running time or memory grows with input size n. O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) one loop, O(n log n) good sorting, O(n^2) nested loops.
A compiler translates the whole program to machine code before running (C, C++). An interpreter runs it line by line (Python). Java compiles to bytecode that the JVM runs.

patterns: how do i fix errors in my code
responses: Debugging means finding and fixing bugs. Error types: syntax (wrong grammar), runtime (crashes while running), logical (wrong output). Tips: read the error message, add print statements, use a debugger, and test small parts.
An API lets programs talk to each other. A REST API uses HTTP methods (GET read, POST create, PUT update, DELETE remove) and usually returns JSON, a text format of key-value pairs.
C is fast and low-level, C++ adds OOP, Java is portable and widely used in enterprise and Android, Python is easy and great for AI, JavaScript powers websites. The best language depends on your goal.
Frontend = what users see (HTML structure, CSS styling, JavaScript behaviour, React). Backend = server logic and database (Python, Node.js, Java). A full-stack developer does both.

patterns: what is computer science and engineering
responses: CSE (Computer Science and Engineering) covers programming, data structures, algorithms, DBMS, operating systems, computer networks, computer architecture, software engineering, AI/ML and theory of computation.
An operating system manages hardware and software resources: processes, memory, files and devices. Examples: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android. The kernel is its core part.

A process is a running program with its own memory. A thread is a lightweight unit inside a process that shares memory. Scheduling decides which process gets the CPU, and a context switch saves and restores its state.

Deadlock is when processes wait for each other forever. Four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait. Semaphores and mutexes control access to shared resources and prevent race conditions.

Memory management allocates RAM to processes. Paging splits memory into fixed-size pages; segmentation uses logical parts. Virtual memory uses disk to extend RAM. Cache is small, very fast memory near the CPU. RAM is volatile, ROM is permanent.

A database stores organised data and a DBMS manages it. RDBMS stores data in tables. Primary key uniquely identifies a row; foreign key links to another table. An ER diagram shows entities and their relationships.

patterns: what is a join in sql
responses: SQL is the language for relational databases. SELECT * FROM students WHERE age > 18; reads data. Groups: DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), DCL (GRANT, REVOKE). JOINs combine tables: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL.

Normalization organises tables to remove redundancy: 1NF (atomic values), 2NF (no partial dependency), 3NF (no transitive dependency), BCNF (stricter). ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability for safe transactions.

MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite are relational (SQL) databases. MongoDB is a NoSQL document database storing JSON-like data. Redis is a very fast in-memory store. SQLite is built into Python and perfect for small projects.
A computer network connects devices to share data. Types: LAN (local), MAN (city), WAN (wide, like the internet). Devices: router, switch, hub, modem. A protocol is a set of communication rules.

OSI has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application. TCP/IP has 4. TCP is reliable and ordered (web, email); UDP is faster but unreliable (video calls, games).
HTTP is the web's protocol (HTTPS adds encryption). DNS turns domain names into IP addresses. An IP address identifies a device. A web server delivers pages to your browser when you open a URL.

Cloud computing rents computing power over the internet (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). IaaS = infrastructure, PaaS = platform (Render, Heroku), SaaS = software (Gmail). Deployment means putting your app online.

Cybersecurity protects systems and data. Encryption scrambles data so only key holders can read it (symmetric = one key, asymmetric = public and private keys). A firewall filters network traffic; phishing tricks people into giving secrets.

Blockchain is a shared, tamper-resistant ledger of linked blocks (used by Bitcoin). IoT connects everyday devices to the internet. Big data means datasets too large for normal tools. Quantum computing uses qubits.

The CPU runs instructions using the ALU (maths and logic), control unit and registers, following the fetch-decode-execute cycle. A GPU handles many parallel tasks (graphics, AI). RISC uses simple instructions, CISC uses complex ones.

patterns: how to convert decimal to binary
what is a bit and byte
responses: Computers use binary (0 and 1). 8 bits = 1 byte. Decimal 5 is binary 101. Hexadecimal is base 16. Logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) combine bits and are the building blocks of circuits. In Python: bin(5).

Software engineering is building software systematically. SDLC phases: requirements, design, coding, testing, deployment, maintenance. Models: Waterfall (step by step) and Agile/Scrum (short iterations). DevOps and CI/CD automate build, test and release.

Theory of Computation studies what computers can solve: finite automata (DFA/NFA), grammars, pushdown automata and Turing machines. Compiler design covers lexical analysis, parsing, and code generation.

Git tracks changes in your code. Workflow:
git init
git add .
git commit -m "message"
git push
Other: git clone, git pull, git branch, git merge, git status.

patterns: how to upload project to github
responses: GitHub hosts Git repositories online for backup, sharing and teamwork. Create a repo, then push your code. Pull request = ask to merge your changes; fork = your own copy of someone's repo.

Editors and IDEs: VS Code (light, popular), PyCharm (full Python IDE), Jupyter Notebook and Google Colab (run code in cells, great for data science and ML), Anaconda (Python plus data-science tools in one installer).
The terminal runs text commands. Basics: cd (change folder), ls or dir (list files), mkdir (new folder), rm (delete), cp (copy), pwd (where am I). Linux is a free, open-source OS popular for servers.
Docker packages an app with everything it needs into a container so it runs the same anywhere. A virtual machine includes a full OS, so containers are lighter. Kubernetes manages many containers.

Handy developer tools: Postman (test APIs), Git and GitHub (version control), Stack Overflow (answers to coding questions), npm and pip (package managers), Docker (containers), AI assistants like Claude and Copilot (help write and explain code).

patterns: what is a program in computer
responses: A computer is an electronic machine that takes input, processes it and gives output. Hardware = the physical parts (CPU, RAM, disk, keyboard, monitor). Software = the programs that run on it: system software (Windows, Linux) and application software (browser, games). Firmware is permanent software stored inside hardware.

Data is raw facts such as numbers, text or images (for example: 45, 60, 72). Information is data that has been processed to give meaning (for example: "the class average is 59"). Data can be structured (tables, SQL) or unstructured (images, videos, free text).

patterns: what is a web browser used for
responses: A website is a collection of web pages you open in a browser. A web app is an interactive website that works like software (Gmail, this chatbot). responses: Basic programming terms: syntax = the grammar rules of a language. Keywords = reserved words like if, for, def. Operators = symbols like + - * / == and. Comments = notes ignored by the computer (# in Python). Identifier = a name you give to a variable or function. Constant = a value that should not change. A library = ready-made code you reuse.
